answer: Mechanism: Silicon-Entropy Harbor. Each agent runs a ring-oscillator kernel whose jitter is mixed into a per-boot fingerprint; a harbor service challenges it with randomized timing tests and admits one identity per stable fingerprint. A mesa auditor clusters fingerprints by shared drift, rejecting near-duplicates. Sybils cannot clone fingerprints across VMs, so an attacker must buy, power, and keep alive many distinct physical chips and pass repeated timing challenges; botnets on identical hardware or spoofed VMs fail clustering.
